P5.gap_analysis: The staleness monitor is a roadmap deliverable, not an acceptance criterion. P5's acceptance criteria (selection reproducible from registry; global install rejected) are both met. The gap does not block P8 but is tracked as a partial dependency.
P5.p8_dependency: P8 does not directly depend on the staleness monitor. P8 depends on P5's selection workflow and provenance records, which are complete.

P6.p8_dependency: P8 must use a technology with readiness SUFFICIENT. TECH-PYTHON-STDLIB is SUFFICIENT. TECH-SPS-CMS is NOT selectable without further research.

P7.p8_dependency: P8 must remain project-local, isolated, and rollback-safe per P7 governance.

candidates.relevance: Implementation language for SPS 2.0 core, governance, validators, and P8 reference implementation
candidates.evidence: sps2/research/cache.json — all 10 coverage areas COVERED, sources rank 2
candidates.notes: Already the foundation for all SPS 2.0 code. P8 will use Python stdlib for the reference implementation.

candidates.relevance: Legacy CMS skill; candidate source for CMS 2.0 patterns
candidates.notes: NOT selectable for P8 without further research. The legacy skill is a template-based system, not a CMS architecture. P8 requires a new architecture, not a port of the legacy skill. KI-01 (hardcoded secret) is classified NEVER COPY.

technology_assessment.gap: No existing technology candidate is a suitable CMS architecture for P8. TECH-PYTHON-STDLIB is SUFFICIENT as the implementation language, but P8 needs a CMS architecture pattern (content model, role separation, asset pipeline) that does not yet exist in the research cache.
technology_assessment.required_action: P8 Phase 2 must research and select a CMS architecture pattern. This may involve: (a) researching an existing open-source CMS architecture for reference patterns, or (b) designing a new architecture from first principles with documented evidence. No technology capability may be invented or inferred.

requirements.title: Super Admin / Admin role separation
requirements.objective: Implement a role-based access control system where Super Admin has full structural control and Admin has content-only access.
acceptance_criteria: Super Admin can create, modify, and delete content types, sections, and layout structure
Admin can create, edit, and publish content within existing structure only
Admin cannot modify layout, section structure, or content types
Role assignments are enforced on every operation
An operation attempted by an unauthorised role is rejected with a controlled message
security_implications: Role escalation prevention: Admin must not be able to self-promote to Super Admin
Every authorisation decision must be logged for audit
Role checks must be server-side, not client-side only

requirements.title: Content and section model
requirements.objective: Define a typed content model with sections that can be composed into pages without hardcoding.
acceptance_criteria: Content types are defined in schema, not hardcoded in templates
Sections are composable and reorderable by Super Admin
Every content field has a defined type and validation rule
Content can be previewed before publishing
Draft and published states are separate
security_implications: Content injection: all user-supplied content must be sanitised
Schema changes must be versioned to prevent breaking existing content

requirements.title: Unified asset picker
requirements.objective: Provide a single asset picker that supports upload, existing media library, and external URL sources.
acceptance_criteria: Upload: file is validated (type, size), virus-scanned if possible, and stored locally
Existing media: user can browse and select from previously uploaded assets
External URL: URL is validated, fetched, optimised, and stored locally (not hotlinked)
All three sources produce a uniform asset reference
Asset metadata (alt text, dimensions, size) is captured and editable

verification.verifier: asset picker integration test + negative tests for each source

security_implications: External URL fetching must prevent SSRF (server-side request forgery)
Upload must enforce file type and size limits
Assets must be stored locally, not hotlinked to external servers
No hardcoded secrets or credentials in asset configuration (KI-01 forbidden)

requirements.title: Preview and publishing workflow
requirements.objective: Enable content authors to preview changes before publishing, and publish with audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: Draft content is visible in preview mode but not in production
Publishing transitions content from draft to published atomically
Every publish action is recorded in audit history with actor, timestamp, and change summary
Unpublish is possible and also audited

verification.verifier: publishing workflow test + audit log verification

security_implications: Preview must not be accessible to unauthorised users

requirements.title: Audit history
requirements.objective: Maintain a complete, append-only audit trail of all CMS operations.
acceptance_criteria: Every create, update, delete, publish, and role change is recorded
Audit entries include actor, action, target, timestamp, and before/after state
Audit log cannot be modified or deleted through the CMS API
Audit log is exportable for compliance review

verification.verifier: audit log completeness test + tamper-evidence test

security_implications: Audit log is a security control — it must be tamper-evident
No credential values may appear in audit entries

requirements.title: Project-local isolation and rollback safety
requirements.objective: P8 must remain project-local, isolated per P7 governance, and removable without modifying SPS2 core.
acceptance_criteria: All P8 state lives inside the repository under domain/cms/
P8 does not write machine-global state
P8 does not modify SPS2 core, governance, or adapter surfaces
P8 can be removed by deleting domain/cms/ and reverting the feature flag
P8 validators pass on a fresh clone with P8 removed
security_implications: P8 must not introduce cross-project state sharing
P8 must not depend on hidden machine-global memory

requirements.title: KI-01 forbidden: no hardcoded secrets
requirements.objective: P8 must not copy or reintroduce the KI-01 hardcoded secret mechanism from the legacy CMS.
acceptance_criteria: No hardcoded secret, token, or credential exists anywhere in P8 code
All secrets are injected via environment variables or a secrets manager
A secret-detection validator scans P8 code and fails on any hardcoded credential pattern
The legacy KI-01 pattern (hardcoded secret fallback in auth helper) is explicitly documented as forbidden
security_implications: This is a CRITICAL security requirement. KI-01 is classified NEVER COPY in the migration matrix.

requirements.title: CONF-001 preserved: no LCP/INP invention
requirements.objective: P8 must not invent, infer, or introduce LCP or INP numeric thresholds. CONF-001 remains UNRESOLVED.
acceptance_criteria: No LCP or INP numeric threshold appears anywhere in P8 code or configuration
If P8 includes performance monitoring, it records observed values without comparing to invented thresholds
CONF-001 remains recorded as UNRESOLVED in all P8 documentation

verification.verifier: regex scan for LCP/INP numeric values in P8 artefacts

security_implications: Inventing performance thresholds would encode unverified facts into the system
This is a governance boundary, not a technical limitation

Design a new architecture from first principles with documented evidence

Python stdlib + a lightweight web framework (requires research)
